elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1(d) requires RevMed to “defend” Sanofi against Third Party Claims alleging that use of the RevMed Licensed Technology or contemplated Research, Development, Manufacture, or Commercialization infringes or misappropriates third-party intellectual property rights. This is a transaction-specific equivalent of coverage for services or deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against losses arising from third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 requires RevMed to “indemnify” Sanofi against Third Party Claims and resulting Losses, and subsection (d) expressly covers infringement and misappropriation allegations involving the licensed technology and contemplated activities.

elements.element: Vendor's defense and indemnification obligations must extend to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The defined “Sanofi Indemnitees” expressly include Sanofi and its Affiliates, together with specified representatives.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The clause covers RevMed's material breach of the Agreement or an Ancillary Agreement, but does not expressly cover breach of law. It is not demonstrable from the rendered language that every applicable-law breach is necessarily a material contractual breach.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against losses arising from third-party claims based on Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: No express breach-of-law indemnity trigger appears. The general material-contractual-breach trigger is not an assured substitute.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No data-breach or Vendor-causation trigger is included.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against losses arising from third-party claims based on a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No data-breach or Vendor-causation indemnity is included.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is not an express indemnity trigger.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against losses arising from third-party claims based on Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is not an express indemnity trigger.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct is not an express indemnity trigger.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against losses arising from third-party claims based on Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct is not an express indemnity trigger.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer to notify Vendor of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no notice procedure.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give Vendor control of the defense and settlement of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: Although RevMed has a duty to defend, the clause does not allocate control of the defense or settlement.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer to reasonably cooperate with Vendor in defending an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: No cooperation obligation appears.

elements.element: Any indemnity given by Customer must be limited exclusively to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: No Customer indemnity appears in the rendered language, so the condition that would require limiting such an indemnity is demonstrably absent from the provided clause.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1(d) expressly requires RevMed to defend Sanofi against third-party infringement or misappropriation claims involving the licensed technology and contemplated activities.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against losses arising from third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1(d), together with the opening language of Section 14.1, provides an express indemnity for Third Party Claims and resulting Losses based on infringement or misappropriation.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by Customer's modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for Customer modifications is included.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by Customer's combination of the services or deliverables with other items.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion is included.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement resulting from Vendor's compliance with Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specifications exclusion is included.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must have an express remedy option to procure Customer's continued right to use the affected item.
elements.evidence: No procurement-of-rights remedy appears.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must have an express remedy option to modify the affected item so that it is non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No modification remedy appears.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must have an express remedy option to replace the affected item with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: No replacement remedy appears.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must have an express remedy option to refund the applicable fees if the other remedies are unavailable or unsuccessful.
elements.evidence: No refund remedy appears.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no indemnity cap or reference to a three-times-annual-fees super-cap.

result.reason: The redline adds a clear, transaction-specific third-party IP defense and indemnity benefiting Sanofi and its Affiliates. It does not implement the other preferred triggers or any claims procedure. It also omits every fallback exclusion, infringement remedy, and the 3× annual-fees super-cap. Because neither level is complete, the redline is not minimal as defined. The added indemnity can coexist with the non-infringement warranty disclaimer as a separate risk-allocation obligation and does not negate the retained contractual-breach indemnity, so unrelated intent is preserved.
